# Preface {.unnumbered}

This book is an introduction to ecological data analysis using the
[Julia](https://julialang.org) language. It began as an answer to a simple question:
*how much of the ecologist's toolkit already exists in Julia today, and how much still
has to be built?*

The obvious reference point is [**Análises Ecológicas no R**](https://analises-ecologicas.com/)
[@silva2022analises] by Silva, Gonçalves-Souza, Paterno, Provete and Vancine — an open,
Portuguese-language book that became the entry point for a generation of Brazilian
ecologists. This volume deliberately follows its structure, chapter by chapter, so the
two can be read side by side.

## Scope of this edition {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-important}
## What this book covers — and what it doesn't yet

This first edition runs **from language basics through generalized linear models**
(chapters 1–9), with a chapter on exploratory data analysis before the models, followed
by two chapters on programming for ecology: writing your own functions and resampling
and simulation (chapters 10–11). The community-ecology chapters of the original book — multivariate
analysis, rarefaction, richness estimators, taxonomic, phylogenetic and functional
diversity, and geospatial data — **are not included**.

That is not an oversight. In R those chapters rest on `vegan`, `iNEXT`, `picante` and
`FD`. Julia has no mature equivalents today. Writing those chapters honestly means
writing the packages first, and that is a separate project. See @sec-limits for a
detailed assessment.
:::

This is not a small slice. They cover what most of an ecological analysis
actually consumes: importing and cleaning data, visualizing it, fitting linear and
generalized linear models, and handling hierarchical structure through mixed models.
At every one of those points the Julia ecosystem is solid: the packages exist, they
are maintained, and they do the work. Where this book compares Julia to R, the
comparisons are limited to what can be checked — syntax, feature coverage, behaviour
demonstrable in the code — and not to performance claims I do not measure here.

## How to use this book {.unnumbered}

All code is executable and runs in the Julia environment defined by `Project.toml`.
To reproduce the book locally:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/esantos2ua/EcologicalAnalysesInJulia.git
cd EcologicalAnalysesInJulia
julia --project=. scripts/setup.jl
quarto render en
```

Throughout the text, boxes like this one translate from R's idiom into Julia's:

::: {.r-equivalent}
**In R**

`dplyr::filter(data, height > 10)` corresponds to `@filter(data, height > 10)` in
`TidierData.jl`. The semantics are the same; the difference is that `@filter` is a
macro rather than a function.
:::

## Relationship to *Análises Ecológicas no R* {.unnumbered}

This project is **inspired by** *Análises Ecológicas no R* [@silva2022analises], by
Fernando Rodrigues da Silva, Thiago Gonçalves-Souza, Gustavo Brant Paterno, Diogo
Borges Provete and Maurício Humberto Vancine, and owes it an explicit structural debt:
this book's chapter sequence deliberately follows theirs, so the two can be read side
by side.

What this book does **not** do is reproduce the original's content. The text, examples,
dataset and exercises here are written from scratch for Julia. The authors of the
original book have no involvement in this project, have not reviewed it, and do not
endorse it; any errors here are mine.

*Análises Ecológicas no R* is freely available at <https://analises-ecologicas.com/>
under a CC BY-NC 4.0 licence, and in print from Nupeea and Canal 6 (2022, 640 pp.,
ISBN 978-85-7917-564-0). If this book is useful to you, the original will probably be
more so.

## Relationship to *ecoR* {.unnumbered}

Chapters 7, 10 and 11 do not come from *Análises Ecológicas no R*. They are **inspired
by** the exploratory-analysis, programming and resampling modules of **ecoR** [@oliveira_ecor], the R course wiki
of the Instituto de Biociências, Universidade de São Paulo, produced and maintained by
Alexandre Adalardo de Oliveira, and based in part on material by João Luis Ferreira
Batista and Paulo Inácio K. L. Prado. As with the original book, the text, examples and
exercises here are written from scratch; the authors of ecoR have not reviewed this
book. Each of the three chapters opens with links to the corresponding ecoR material.

ecoR is freely available at <https://ecor.ib.usp.br/> under a CC BY-SA 4.0 licence,
with exercises graded automatically in [notaR](http://notar.ib.usp.br).

## Bilingual edition {.unnumbered}

This book exists in English and Portuguese, built from the same repository. The
Portuguese version is at [`/pt`](../pt/). The chapters are translations of one
another, and the code is identical in both.
